items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to more
closely align the privileges of farm distilleries with other privileges
enjoyed by farmers
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5853

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law,
in relation to more closely align the privileges of farm distilleries
with other privileges enjoyed by farmers

 PURPOSE :

To allow farm breweries, cideries, distilleries, and wineries to cross
promote each others' products and to share a more similar set of
privileges under the law.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Amends subdivision five of section 25 of section 3 of the
alcohol and beverage control law.

Section 2: Amends subparagraphs (v), (vi), and (vii) of paragraph (a)
of subdivision 2-c of section 61 of the alcoholic beverage control
law.

Section 3: Amends subparagraph (e), of subdivision 2-c of section 61
of the alcoholic beverage control law.

Section 4: Amends subparagraphs (e) and (f), of subdivision 2 of
section 76-a of the alcoholic beverage control law.

Section 5: Amends subparagraphs (e)-(h) of subdivision 6 of section
76-a of the alcoholic beverage control law.

Section 6: Amends subparagraphs (f), (h), (i), and (j) of subdivision
2 of section 58-c of the alcoholic beverage control law.

Section 7: Amends subparagraphs (e)-(1) of subdivision 2 of section
51-a of the alcoholic beverage control law.

Section 8: States that the act shall take effect ninety days after
this bill shall have become law.

 JUSTIFICATION :

New York State has seen dramatic job growth at small farm breweries,
wineries and distilleries over the past seven years thanks to
legislative efforts to encourage investment in "buy local" economic
development efforts. A major reason for the success of some of the
country's best brewery, distillery, and winery trails has been the
result of close collaboration and cross promotion by regional farms,
wineries, breweries, and distilleries. These trails celebrate the
unique cultural heritage, natural beauty, and agricultural products of
their host region by linking all stages of production into one visitor
experience. Such collaboration allows locals and tourists alike to
experience all the facets of their favorite beverage's creation and
more.

However, in New York State the ability for regional producers to
collaborate is limited. The laws that govern the production and retail
licenses extended to farm breweries, wineries, cideries, and
distilleries does not give each type of producer the same ability to
sell or otherwise cross promote other New York State labelled or farm
produced products. Their ability to cross promote different types of
products is also limited to varying degrees depending on the type of
licensee. By more closely aligning the privileges extended to each
license type with each other, this bill will help New York State's
regional and craft alcoholic beverage producers to cross promote and
collaborate in new ways that were previously only available to out of
state competitors. Allowing individual producers to find new ways to
work together to promote and sell each others' products will help each
to grow their business and will encourage tourism statewide.  Also,
because this bill targets farm licensees, any growth in their
businesses will also grow the market for those New York State farm
products that are needed for the production of alcoholic beverages.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect within 90 days.

summary: Relates to expanding the privileges of farm breweries, cideries, wineries and distilleries to allow for the sales of "farm brewed" alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption.
